properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony and Alex, 2026-09-08, in dialogue. Anthony: "It really bothers me that you have to use a 'translate' skill at your work in order for it to work with reflow2… My hope is that you shouldn't need a 'translator' skill. If it turns out I do need an additional skill, then taking what you define in your translator skill should be added directly to all reflow2 itself." Alex: "Some of it is just explaining how I want it to be digested since reflow is being added after the fact. But also, I think partly for consistency."

═══ THE FIRST THING TO SAY IS THAT THIS WAS ALREADY DECIDED, AND HALF-BUILT ═══

`dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` was ACCEPTED on 2026-08-14, on Alex's first-run report, ordering BOTH a served interview step AND a served routing table. Both shipped. `cap:the-design-interview-precedes-the-capture` reads `realized`. So the honest answer to "why didn't reflow2 define these boxes?" is NOT that nobody thought of it — it is that what shipped answers a different question from the one Alex is asking.

⭐⭐ MEASURED 2026-09-08, AND THIS IS THE FINDING: THE ROUTING TABLE IS KEYED ON ENGLISH PHRASING, NOT ON DOMAIN NOUNS. Every row of the table in `capture-intent` is a grammatical construction — "it has to…", "the X part", "where X meets Y", "first this, then that", a number with a unit. There is not one domain word in it. It routes HOW SOMEBODY SAID IT.

Alex's problem is the other axis. The earlier node's worked example was a domain's first-class thing behaving like a request against a structured body of records, for which Interface, Capability, Requirement and Flow were ALL defensible. No phrasing row reaches that, because the question is not "what does 'it has to' mean" but "what IS a query, in our world." **A table that routes grammar cannot answer a question about nouns, and that is a clean split rather than a shortfall in coverage.**

═══ AND THE TRANSLATOR IS DOING AT LEAST THREE JOBS ═══

Alex named three reasons in one sentence and they are not the same kind of thing:

**(1) "since reflow is being added after the fact" — BROWNFIELD.** This is the `adopt` skill's territory, and the routing table lives in `capture-intent`, which is the greenfield capture path. A system that already exists needs its existing parts named before anything is captured; that is a different act from routing a sentence someone just said.

**(2) "partly for consistency" — HOUSE STYLE.** He wants repeated captures to come out the same way. Nothing in reflow2 records a project's OWN conventions — how this team names things, which distinctions it always draws. That is neither vocabulary nor adoption; it is a per-project convention with no home.

**(3) The domain-noun mapping** — partly served, keyed on the wrong axis, as above.

Only (3) is even partly what the accepted decision was about. **A single skill absorbing all three is exactly why it is hard to say whether reflow2 should own it.**

═══ THE BLACK-BOX FRAME, TAKEN SERIOUSLY, CUTS BOTH WAYS ═══

Anthony's own doctrine says a seam between two boxes needs a stated contract. Alex's translator IS that contract — between his organisation's vocabulary and reflow2's. By that doctrine the adapter existing is not a defect; **the open question is whose box it lives in.**

And there is a virtue underneath it that must not be traded away. reflow2 deliberately refuses to infer: `dec:ask-not-repair`, no fabricated repair, detecting is not asking. A statement like "in our world a query is an Interface" is precisely the kind of thing reflow2 must NOT guess. **So the need for a stated mapping is created by a virtue, not by a gap.** What is missing is not the guess — it is a PLACE TO PUT THE ANSWER, so the mapping is design data the graph holds rather than a private skill each user reinvents.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) DO NOTHING — the translator is a legitimate project-local adapter.** Cheapest, and defensible under the black-box doctrine. ⚠️ Counter: every user rebuilds it, badly, and nothing can check it. Alex's mapping might contain a category error that surfaces in six months, and reflow2 would never know.

**(b) ABSORB IT WHOLESALE into reflow2 — Anthony's stated hope.** ⚠️ Counter, and it is the strong one: this generalises from ONE translator, written by an EARLY ADOPTER, in ONE domain. Anthony has caught this project reasoning from a prevalence count before. Absorbing a domain-specific glossary into a domain-neutral tool is how SE vocabulary stops spanning a house and a spacecraft.

**(c) MAKE THE MAPPING FIRST-CLASS AND RECORDABLE — a per-project glossary the DESIGN holds.** The user states "in our world, X is a Component" once; reflow2 records it, applies it, and can later show it back and check it for collisions. Keeps the never-guess virtue AND kills the out-of-band skill. ⚠️ Counter: new vocabulary for a problem measured on one or two users; and it risks becoming the framework registry that `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` was correctly DROPPED for being — cosmetic renaming that gates nothing. The distinction to hold is that a glossary must map to the UNCHANGED node types and gate NO computation.

**(d) FIX THE ADOPTION PATH INSTEAD.** If reason (1) dominates, the routing table belongs in `adopt` as much as in `capture-intent`, and a brownfield system needs its parts named before its sentences are routed. ⚠️ Counter: does nothing for reasons (2) or (3).

**(e) A CONVENTIONS RECORD.** If reason (2) dominates, what is missing is a place for "how we do it here" — which the routing table's own last row already admits reflow2 has no home for: *"this is how we do X here — Nothing fits cleanly."* ⚠️ Counter: smallest of the options and the least likely to be what bothers Anthony.

**(f) MEASURE FIRST, AND THIS IS THE RECOMMENDED FIRST MOVE.** The deciding question is cheap and unanswered: **do translators from DIFFERENT projects say the same thing or different things?** If the same — reflow2 is missing something general and (b) or (c) is right. If different — it is project-local and (c) is right in a weaker form, or (a) is. **One translator cannot distinguish these.** Anthony has already asked Alex for a pseudo-project, which is exactly the right instrument; the sharpening is to ask for the TRANSLATOR ITSELF, generalised, from two or three projects rather than one.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

Diff two or three translators. Rows that recur across domains belong in reflow2. Rows that do not belong in a per-project glossary. **Nobody has done that, and until it is done every option above is an argument rather than a finding.**

⚠️ AND ONE HONEST LIMIT ON EVERYTHING ABOVE: this is a relayed second-hand account of Alex's reasoning. His actual translator has not been read. The three-jobs split is inferred from one sentence he wrote, and he may say it is wrong.
properties.name: OPEN — the routing table that shipped routes ENGLISH PHRASING, not domain NOUNS, and a user's translator is doing at least three jobs of which only one is reflow2's
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: the ideas enter as ideas, nothing is promoted, and the objection sits beside each rather than replacing it.

AN AGENT'S READING, offered as a finding rather than an answer. The single most useful thing here is not an option — it is the measurement that the shipped routing table routes GRAMMAR and Alex's question is about NOUNS. That reframes "reflow2 failed to define the boxes" into "reflow2 answered a different question well," which is a much better starting point and was not visible until the table was actually read.

The second most useful thing is that Alex's one sentence contains three different problems. Any solution aimed at "the translator" as a single object will over-serve two of them and under-serve one.

Anthony's instinct that a translator should not be necessary is worth taking seriously AND worth resisting in one specific way: reflow2's refusal to infer is what creates the need for a stated mapping. Removing the need for a translator by making reflow2 guess would trade a load-bearing virtue for a convenience, and that trade should be made deliberately if at all.
